utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I must first remind you, Mr. Forand, that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: General Forand, we're going to look at some documents now concerning freedom of movement and how that progressed between you and Mr. Cermak, as well as other factors that had a play in this matter. The first document that I would like you to look at is P347. And the page that we need to turn to on this is, first of all, the first page, where you say in your sitrep that: "The HV are restricting our movement."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's the wrong -- that's not the same document that I have for that. My mistake. Hang on. Second page. It's the letter. A bit of confusion because this is -- exists as a stand-alone document, as well as being part of a sitrep, so it's difficult to trace it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the letter that you wrote to General Gotovina which we looked at yesterday and the day before, concerning your request for a meeting with the military governor; but then in paragraph 2: "The restriction on freedom of movement in Sector South must be lifted immediately," which was something that you wanted so that you could get out of your camp; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. You refer in another document, 65 ter 1607, on the 5th of August, in paragraph 1, fourth line: "The HV are restricting our movement, although we have had authority from one set of Croatian army liaison officers to proceed with patrolling and humanitarian assistance." Then they got blocked having gone less than a kilometre. First of all, can you recollect which Croatian army liaison officers had given permission to proceed, where they were based or what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the blocking of the patrol, can you remember where that was?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the content of that first paragraph, it must have been from my headquarters, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. So that would have been out of the UNCRO compound in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, from my headquarters in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. So someone had let them through at the gate, but they hadn't got any further than a kilometre?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose there must have been discussion with that CALO, whoever he may have been, either on the phone or verbally, that we were, according to him, from what I'm reading, given the permission to get out of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Can we look at page 2 of this document, paragraph B: "I'm pressing wherever I can for freedom of movement, for humanitarian relief, monitoring military activity. I understand that a Croatian army liaison office team is being dispatched here from Zadar, and I've offered that space in my HQ to facilitate." Is that the reference there that you are referring to offering a space to Marine Lukovic, Captain Lukovic, in your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I don't know if it was specifically for Captain Lukovic, but I know that we had offered a space within my headquarters for a liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D317 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have a 65 ter number 1654, 1654, for the next document. That's 347, Prosecution Exhibit 347.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Still taking up the account on this, on the 5th of August, and you were calling for intervention of senior officials at every level to try and reestablish your freedom of movement which was fundamentally important to you. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And I've just put this in. We've looked at it before just so that the whole chain of it is able to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Next document I'd like to turn to is 65 ter 1625.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is another sitrep for the 6th of August, 1995. It may have been a Prosecution exhibit. I've just flag that up. Here, you can see in paragraph 1: "Immediate concerns with respect to the current situation in Knin and Sector South. I will be discussing those points at my level with the Croatian liaison office in Knin; however, I would appreciate if those points were discussed with Croat authorities in Zagreb." At your level with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are reading from an English text, and we have at this moment on our screen a B/C/S text and not a corresponding page for the English text. And what we just saw apparently as the second page seems not to correspond --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with what you're reading, because I saw a very short, and I see it now again. I see a paragraph 2 and a paragraph 3, where in the original we have a short paragraph 1 and then a longer paragraph 2. So these are not corresponding documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My apologies for that. That is my responsibility. The ERN number that I'm looking at is 0052-7776, if that may help the situation. I've read it out to you accurately, you can take that from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take that from you; but at the same time, the Chamber would like to know what document we are dealing with. It seems that, Mr. Registrar ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can describe it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, at the inconsistency, or at least the discrepancy, between original and translation is apparently caused by the way in which you have uploaded these documents, because I do understand that these documents are uploaded by the OTP. So if you would please have a look at that. Meanwhile, Mr. Kay, if you would be very precise in describing what the document exactly is; and if you would have a hard copy, that might assist the witness because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'll give the witness my copy, as I can deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I apologise for the markings in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... You can see where we've got our information from. Thank you, Mr. Usher, that's the spot on point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was going to ask you, having read it out, that your level with the Croat liaison office in Knin, what you meant by that? What was your level with the Croat liaison office in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be a reference to the other sitrep, where I was saying that the Croat liaison was coming from Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. And the passage below, "HV soldiers are claiming that this imposed restriction of movement is for our own security," where did that information come from?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that must have been with discussion, you know, with soldiers that were at the gate of my headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we could just turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you go to the pink passage which has helpfully been marked in advance, paragraph 7. "I am seeking your support to resolve the foregoing points with the Croatian authorities as a matter of priority," indicating, would you agree, that you wanted RHQ in Zagreb to assist you in resolving these issues?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that document, subject to it being correctly identified as to what it is, could be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although, I have seen this document before; I know that for sure. So, therefore, Mr. Registrar, if you would please make a note that it may be that this document needs a number; and that, meanwhile, everyone is invited to find it on the already existing lists or one of the exhibits. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're now going to look at a document, 2D03-0123. This is a document which is quite long in text, but the relevant part has been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 2 after you have shown the first page, Mr. Monkhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document coming from Brigadier Plestina whom you met, I understand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him once. He came to my camp sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will get there soon on this. This is from him on the 6th of August. And as page 2 shows us, it's minutes of a meeting between chief of the UNCRO staff, Colonel Pettis. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did. He was the Chief of Staff of my UNCRO headquarters; not my, but my superior UNCRO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And he had a meeting with Brigadier Plestina. We can see what the document is about. The second paragraph, last sentence refers to the: "The main problem is total prohibition leaving the facility," meaning your UN compound, so that you can go to the UN warehouse in Knin, "needing supplies." Paragraph 3 refers to a requirement of opening roads to enable communication between UNCRO sector commands and subordinate units on the field; is that right? You needed roads opened so that you could go to your subordinate units elsewhere in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They also require freedom of movement in the area next to those where battles take place in order to report on human rights and similar. Colonel Pettis said that would be useful for Croatia as well. And we note here that request was refused by Brigadier Plestina, saying: "We have been in Knin just one day and the battle has still been carrying on. We expect component UN agencies and not UNCRO military units will report on human rights." Just looking at that passage there, we note Brigadier Plestina refused a request from what would be your headquarters in Zagreb; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seems to be the case because I never saw that -- those minutes by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Were they keeping you informed at HQ Zagreb of refusals that were happening higher up the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember is that we -- the communication were not very good in the sense, no. I think we were not kept aware of all the discussion that was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that something that was a handicap to you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say that was not what I was expecting to see as far as information were ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there an issue about UNCRO, which was the peace force, having a role in monitoring the human rights issues that were of concern to the UN at this time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was an issue, but as far as humanitarian right, if we see something a soldier that is ongoing that is against humanitarian rights, I think it's our duty to report it. But I think you will see that in one of the sitrep, that I explained very clearly to my battalion commanders that our first priority was the dismantling. I think it's somewhere around the 10th or 11th of August, somewhere around there, where it's clearly stated in the sitrep. And when I had my battalion commander, I think it was on the 10th of August at my headquarters, I reiterate that; but I also mentioned that anything that they saw which was against humanitarian rights, I expect that they would document it and report it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the position of the Croatian government that that was not why foreign troops in the form of UNCRO were on their territorial area, that that was not your mandate?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just moving on further in that paragraph, it seems that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, meanwhile, I can inform you that the document you just had on the screen is P348, 65 ter 1994. So there must be a double with 1625. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour, and thank you to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we can see further in that paragraph the issue of communication problems. That's all I need refer you to there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can that document be made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D318, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D318 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document that we are going to look at is 2D03-0169. I believe it hasn't been uploaded yet into the system, Your Honour, so we have copies here for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- the ELMO. It's been put for uploading but it hasn't realised yet. Thank you. This is a partial translation. And if page 4 of the Croatian document can be put on to the -- actually, page 1 first, just so that people can see it. It's a document, again, from Brigadier Plestina, dated the 7th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You can see the date period that it refers to, events between the 6th of August, 7th of August, and it's a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, we now have the original in front of us, and you explain to us without us being able to follow what it is. Do we have copies? Do we have copies of it because you are talking about a partial translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber would like to have whatever copies there are, or to see it on the screen, so that we can follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- because I know that we can only put the English on at this stage, so that other parties could see it. If we put on the English translation now which is on the screen. From this report, we've just translated the Sector South part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You can see the document as described by me which is the extract from page 3 of the Croatian document. It refers there to: "The office of our UNCRO liaison officer has been established ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you give to Mr. Usher more copies than one? Then perhaps Mr. Usher could provide us with a hard copy as well. As soon as I can't manipulate my own material anymore, I get a bit nervous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Is there one available for the Prosecution as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I see that I only received the translation. And if for whatever reason there is not yet a copy uploaded, then at least we should have four copies: One copy for the party dealing with the matter, of course, preferably also for other Defence counsel; one for the ELMO; one for the Bench; and one for the other party. If there is an original, I would like to see it; if not, then I would get it after it has been on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It has been sent in electronic form to the Prosecution, I'm afraid under a different number, because this is the number for the e-court. Your Honour, is it all right for me to proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This, again, is just taking the story further on, and for reference purposes, General Forand: "The office of our UNCRO liaison officer has been established. Three officers from Zadar in the office established liaison with UNCRO command." Is that right that the three officers had established liaison with you by the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. "In the first meeting, General Forand -- with General Forand, they mainly talked about unfounded complaints that UNCRO filed regarding the restriction of movement. Our liaison officer explained to General Forand that UNCRO has complete freedom of movement regarding the supply of units on the field, that there is no need for their patrols, observations from the points, and reports on breaching Zagreb agreement." Is that right that the liaison officers of the Croatian army expressed those matters to you in that way as reported in this document?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like I said before, sir, I don't remember, you know, that particular discussion, and I don't remember ever seeing it in one of our situation report where we explained that they had been at that particular meeting. It could have been, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit? And my apologies to the Court for not having copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I'm reasonably confident I will not have an objection, but just out of some procedural matter -- in fact, we did not receive this document. I needed to clarify the record on that. We received an e-mail notification this morning that the Defence might be using a document under that particular number, but not the document itself. So I simply want to look it over, and I have not yet had the chance to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we already assign it a number to it. Would it be agreeable, because otherwise we get a long MFI list, that the document will be admitted into evidence but that you have an opportunity to revisit the matter within today or tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's absolutely fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D319 is admitted into evidence under the proviso that, first of all, that it will be uploaded into e-court, and we are talking about a daily report of the 6th of August, 1995 to the 7th of August, 1995. And the second proviso is that the Prosecution has an opportunity to restate its position until Friday. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Next in the chain, but we're not going to pull up the exhibit, but it's Exhibit 359.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You recollect you had a meeting with General Gotovina at the Knin Castle where you recorded that he talked to you about freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And he didn't ask you for your opinion on the matter, but told you what the situation was going to be from his position; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what was reflected in the situation report, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And Exhibit 359 also records that maps were going to be provided to you showing the areas that were safe to travel. That's what he said to you.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that part, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's look at Exhibit P359, and if we could go to page 3 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the situation report produced through you by the Prosecution of the 8th of August, 2030 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of paragraph 3, if that can be produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see there the text?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You weren't asked for your opinion, you were told that it was concern for your safety, and that maps would be provided showing the areas that were safe to travel.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that the travel should be confined to main public roads due to mine hazard. And you asked permission to bring your COs to Knin, and you were told to use the coastal highway. And later on that day, you had, at 1.00, a meeting with General Cermak, and also the freedom of movement was again discussed by you in detail. And you were told by him, paragraph 3(1), it's recorded he would give orders that you would be allowed to travel freely within Knin and Drnis. That's how it was expressed to you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can move now from that exhibit, and go to the next document which is -- I have as Prosecution Exhibit 65 ter 2735. I know it's been an exhibit, but again it's the form. Which document it has is difficult to trace. We're looking at now the letter that you received later that day as Mr. Cermak mentioned. And that letter had, as an attachment, a map; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been there. I don't remember. But it's listed that it was there, so it must have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And General Gotovina had said you were going to receive a map, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm just checking that this has been exhibited before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It has. It's part of the -- it was used during the examination in chief, and we're just running the number now to identify the P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: P405, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tieger. The next document I want to look at on this matter is 2D03-0177. Your Honour, again, this is on the ELMO. I believe it's being put into e-court but has yet to be uploaded into the system. It's another document from Brigadier Plestina, dated the 8th of August, 1995 referring to the 7th of August to 8th of August, 1995. That's the front page. Again, the relevant extract has been translated relating to Sector South. If that could be put on the ELMO which is page -- that's Sector North. Next page. That's Sector South. If the English translation could be put on the ELMO now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, before you continue, I see these daily reports. I do not see an addressee of that, to whom. I mean, it's clear that the previous one might be the same for this one. It was signed by Brigadier Budimir Plestina, but to whom it is addressed remains rather unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can see "military secret" on it. It's now released on the e-court system, Your Honour. Would you Your Honour like to proceed to get it off that rather than using the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My real problem was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to whom these reports are addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's fine to have them on my screen but that was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm only as good as my document, I'm afraid, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's a report for whomever. It doesn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's the Ministry of Defence will be where it's going to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where can we see that from the report? You could also say that it's coming from the Ministry Of the Defence. It could be sent to the government, to the President, to the local commanders, to whatever. I don't say any clue as to whom this is addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can't help you, Your Honour. It's a document that comes into my hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're using it as having some relevance; and, of course, it's always good to know not only who drafted it but also where it was sent to. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. These have been very recently received by me, and I've looked at in the last days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This report from Brigadier Plestina, in the second paragraph: "The cooperation of our liaison officers with the UNCRO units on the field has continued." Is that right, was the UNCRO sector cooperation taking place with the Croatian army liaison officers?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember with the unit at my headquarters. Obviously, we had established liaison with General Cermak and his people; but I cannot confirm, from the unit point of view, if that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. It refers here, though, to liaison officers rather than General Cermak. All these documents, General Forand, in fact, exclude General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once General Cermak was in a position, that's with whom we were dealing in my headquarters in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll go further into this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try now to understand, Mr. Kay, what all these documents are about. In the previous one that was provisionally admitted into evidence, the activities of liaison officers are described in the following way. It says: "In the Zadar area, the majority of the activities of our liaison officers is oriented on agreeing with CanBat withdrawal of the CanBat soldiers from the numerous observation points and the security of unobstructed water, toiletries, and foot supply in their foot command in Rastevic." So that part of the description of the liaison officers that is oriented on agreeing with CanBat withdrawal of CanBat soldiers from the numerous observation points, is that what you recognise as far as what happened as far as the units is concerned and as far as the Croatian liaison officers is concerned? Do you agree on that role from observation posts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that particular position, sir. I know that just prior to the 4th of August, the Canadians had sent a liaison officer to Zadar, and that the liaison officer was negotiating with the Croats because some equipment, you know, had been taken from them from certain observation posts. And they were negotiating also the return of certain Canadians that had been taken to Zadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who had been taken or who had withdrawn? I mean, what was the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, taken to Zadar. They were removed from their observation post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And they were escorted back to Zadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, if you say -- if the language of the liaison officers here used is to agree with CanBat withdrawal of the CanBat soldiers from the numerous observation posts, you say, as far as you were aware, that they were taken from the observation posts to Zadar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was during the 4th, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm here talking about the -- this report is about the 6th and the 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that because I don't ever remember the Canadian Battalion reporting to me, you know, that this was taking place. The only time it took place was on the 4th, you know. As the Croat army was advancing, certain of the observation posts that the Canadian had, the same thing for the Kenyans, that they were told, you know, to remove themselves from the observation post. Some of them went back to their unit area; others were brought to Zadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the middle of that sect paragraph, the issue of CanBat refusing radio silence, that was a matter that occurred on the 4th of August; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not only the Canadian Battalion, it was all the units that were reporting; and that memo that we received from Captain Lukovic was addressed to all of my units within Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But could you just answer the question: Was it the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it was the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was the question. I'd like to now turn to another similar document to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can that document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The same situation as the previous document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means this one is now uploaded. So, therefore, I'll immediately check whether we have a translation uploaded as well. Yes. We have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All documents have been uploaded, I am informed now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have the original five-page document in full and a translation on Sector South. Mr. Tieger, the same would then apply that you will have an opportunity until tomorrow, end of the session, to revisit your position as far as admission is concerned. Mr. Registrar, this would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D320 is admitted with the proviso I've just expressed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document, General Forand, again from Brigadier Plestina, dated the 10th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll endeavour to answer Your Honour's question on the direction of these documents during the course of the day, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we can see in this passage on Sector South, reference in the third paragraph to: "UNCRO trying is continue the activities it did till the storm operation started and requires freedom of movement in the whole liberated area. When asked by our liaison officers what the purpose and objective of these patrols is, they answered that they are just soldiers and are still ordered to control the liberated territory." Would you accept that there was a tension between UNCRO and the government of Croatia as to your role now on what was part of the sovereign territory of that state, Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if there was tension because what is highlighted here goes contrary to what I had put on the sitrep and what I had said to my battalion commanders, that our first responsibility was the dismantling of the observation posts which required us to go throughout the sector, because also I wanted to recuperate some of the equipment, you know, that the UN had lost or was not sure where it was. So I had to go through all the sector. In addition to that, what I was telling them is that: If you see any infringement to human rights, it's our duty to report it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The paragraph below the one we've just referred to: "Our liaison officers explained ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, this document apparently speaks about "our liaison officers" frequently. I would be very much interested to know what exactly is meant by that. I don't know whether this witness can help us out who the liaison officers, I take it Croatian liaison officers. But whether these were the liaison officers we know about already or whether there were any other liaison officers is something I'd very much like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The last document in this sequence, I think, will help, Your Honour, in relation to that, and I do have that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the next paragraph: "Our liaison officers explained them that UNCRO has full freedom of movement for supplying camps ... and no reason to patrol." Again, there's a reference to the liaison officers discussing freedom of movement with you. Who would that have been?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said before, the only -- after the 7th, the only discussion I had at my level and the officer from my headquarters were with General Cermak or General Cermak's staff. Now, if the units had some discussion with the liaison officer, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Should we just go to the next page of the document and look carefully at where Brigadier Plestina is from, in terms of his position. The letter is from the Ministry of Defence, Republic of Croatia UN and EU office, and he was the chief of the office. The liaison office was part of -- the Croatian army liaison office was part of the UN and EU office within their military structure; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so. I mean, like I said, I met General Plestina once. I don't even remember what he looked like, but I saw a sitrep that says that I met him at my Sector Headquarters South. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you didn't know that -- where he was within the Croatian army command structure?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May that document be made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, same proviso?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Same situation, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then same decision as well, but, of course, Mr. Registrar, first a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D321, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D321 is admitted into evidence with the proviso that the Prosecution can revisit its position until Friday, end of the session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Next document is Exhibit P390 which is the letter to you, General Forand, from General Cermak, concerning your letter of the 10th of August. We know the terms of this letter, although it always bears looking at again as new issues are looked at. We can see in paragraph 3: UNCRO units being allowed full freedom of movement for the purpose of providing food, drink, and fuel to their bases." And that was the issue concerning what you were able to do within the state of Croatia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was more than that, if you go back to the deal that was signed between Mr. Akashi and the Croatian government. I think we were allowed a little bit more latitude than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking at this document and pulling up from the last question I asked you about the last exhibit, you can see units in area of responsibility, Ministry of Defence, and the office for UN and EU. You still experienced problems with freedom of movement despite that letter as we have seen in the situation reports; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that order of General Cermak, as signed by him, was the document that was issued; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go now to P364.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to understand all the questions. I see that there was a problem where there was a claim for full freedom of movement without restrictions, as far as the purpose is concerned, where only limited freedom of movement was granted; that is, to resupply or to supply good, drinks, fuel. Now, I'm trying to understand your last question: "And that order of General Cermak, as signed by him, was the document that was issued?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Issued as a pass, General Forand, if that clarifies the matter. I believe you said it in evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does that help?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to see. "Issued," you mean this letter was issued as a pass for freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's what we took it for, and I issued it to all my units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the pass was for very limited purposes, isn't it, only if someone was on the way with food, drinks, or fuel. This would help or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But there was also a reference, sir, to Article 4 and 5 of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. So this document as a pass under paragraph 1, we see that it's written that: "Full freedom of movement for UN members mentioned in the agreement." This is a reference to the Akashi agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then: "Full freedom of movement is allowed to UNCRO troops in order to supply themselves with food, drinks, and fuel." Were UNCRO troops not included in the agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was, sir. But I think if you read the agreement, it makes a difference between the United Nations humanitarian rights and the UNCRO people. But there's also under paragraph 5, I remember well, that where we wanted to go was to be in consultation with the HV troops. But my interpretation is that that consultation is not a binding agreement, and that we were still allowed to go wherever we want. But my order to my troops was to dismantle the observation post and to recuperate the equipment that was to the UN in order to concentrate it into area. But at the same time, while they were moving from point A to point B to do that particular function, they were asked to report if they saw anything that went against humanitarian rights. In my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you considered the freedom of movement to UNCRO troops to be broader under the agreement as written down in this letter; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I now better understand what the letter says and what the testimony of the witness is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit D28 is the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. We're under pressure of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can't go through in a way I would like to with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. And most of the times, I think the Chamber understands --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- even in shortened form what the evidence is. And, now and again, it happens that we need to go a bit further. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can go to Exhibit P364 which is the last document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if you turn to page 2 of P364 which is your sitrep of the 12th of August, 1995. If we look at the foot of the page in paragraph 3, we see the report of the meeting with Brigadier Plestina. General, we've looked at the series of documents from Brigadier Plestina how they mesh into this issue of freedom of movement. And you had a meeting with him on the 12th of August, and he was described by you as the head of the office of the UN and ECMM Croatian army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And when he came to see you, did you appreciate that he was the head of the Croatian army liaison officers?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I must have been told at which function he occupied, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And he was visiting Knin from Zagreb. He was with Captain Naval Lukovic, who we've referred to, who was a Croatian army liaison officer. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: CALO, Operation Group South. So he was the Croatian army liaison officer of Operation Group South; Jeffrey Beaumont from headquarters UNCRO, and the Croatian army CSS.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the civilian affairs coordinator. That was Mr. Al-Alfi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I had not seen it written that way before. The tone of the meeting was cordial. You outlined planning for redeployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And expressed concern for looting and theft of equipment which had taken place. Mr. Al-Alfi expressed the need for complete freedom of movement of human rights teams; also requested lists of Serbs killed and wounded to be provided; other issues. And then the last sentence: "Brigadier Plestina pledged full freedom of movement but indicated the other issues were outside his competence." Is it correct that your meeting with Brigadier Plestina, who had come from Zagreb, was on the issue of freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, according to that sitrep, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And his purpose for being there was because he was controlling the issue of freedom of movement between the UNCRO, UN, and the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, isn't that why he was there with Mr. Beaumont from the headquarters of UNCRO?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if he was in charge of controlling the issue, except that we brought it up to him. That's all I can say based on that sitrep because I don't remember that individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And as we've seen from the reports by Brigadier Plestina, he was reporting on how the issue of freedom of movement was being reported by his liaison officers to UNCRO in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, based on what you've shown me, because I have never seen those reports before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And General Cermak, in fact, like you, was a conduit in this matter.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seems to be the case, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That deals with that matter. In your statements, you referred to nothing ever being done about stopping crimes. Were you aware of a number of orders issued by the Ministry of the Interior of the Croatian government to the police officers under their command to stop looting, burning, killing, committing crimes? Were you aware that, during August, orders were issued by the Croatian Ministry of Interior that controlled the police, to police officers, that those crimes you were complaining about should not be happening?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, sir, no, I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Should we look at --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- an exhibit, D46, dated the 10th of August. This is a report from the Assistant Minister of Interior, which controls the police under the Croatian administration, to the head of the military police administration, referring to reports from the field, noting individual Croatian army members on liberated territory stealing, burning houses, killing cattle; and complaining about the lack of cooperation at checkpoints and roadblocks between the police and the military police, and asking for measures to be taken. Were you aware of such matters happening within the Croatian administration of government?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware at all of the concern from the Ministry of Interior about the crimes that were happening as complained of by you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can just look at D48, Exhibit D48.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, it's a report from the MUP to the chief of military police, regarding crimes being committed on the 17th of August, and saying that the perpetrators wearing Croatian army uniforms. That is another example of such an order. Were you being briefed in any way that these steps were being taken within the Croatian government that orders were being issued?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just look at one more document on this matter as an example, 18th of August, Exhibit D49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, also for me to understand this letter, addressed to Mr. Laussic, I see that it's admitted into evidence. Now, who is sending it and who is receiving it? Is it addressed to the military police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's sent to the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Administration to the chief. Now, who sent it? The original and also the translation say that it's about Operation Povratak, which is translated as?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Povratak, "Return," yes. But, usually, we get these nice letterheads, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to again use my time as sparsely as possible. These were documents produced through the witness, Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The cross-examination of Mr. Flynn, I didn't want to repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This gives me guidance. You say I've got the answers there. I hope that you will understand that have not every single page of the transcript on my mind, but I will look at it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm grateful for the Court's inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've just looked at two documents from the Ministry of the Interior, man in charge of the police, to the military police. Now we're looking at a document here, Exhibit D49, from that same man, Josko Moric, to all the police administrations. The Court has heard evidence about this before, General Forand. We see Zadar Knin there, and the Court will be familiar with what that means from the Witness Elleby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 2, please, of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Reports from police stations, police administrations, showing torching of houses, taking property, perpetrated by -- mostly perpetrated by individuals wearing Croatian army uniforms. Issue about whether they are or not. Then we see an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page of the English please, and the next page of the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Police administration chiefs, military -- commanders of military police battalions are told of the problem and decision to put a stop it it. Something, no doubt, you would agree would have been steps that were necessary to be taken; is that right, General Forand?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that meeting between the military police and the civil police, meeting must be informed of the decision that cases of torching of houses and taking property will not be operatively investigated. That's a matter that the Court will be looking at. But a stop must be put to this type of, I put in, "behaviour" as of today. Then a series of measures to be taken relevant to stopping crime. Was that something that you were aware of that was actually in hand by the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I won't go any further into this issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one general question: Were you aware of any similar internal instructions, orders, meetings, et cetera, in order to deal with the matter of crimes being committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to the Croatian army, were you also aware that a series of orders were issued from the Chief of Staff, General Cervenko, as well as from General Gotovina of the Split military district, telling -- ordering that crimes should not be committed?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A there is a mistake on the transcript here, where it says General Cermak, where you said General Cervenko, I think, Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just a question of inadvertence, but to just clarify the record. As the question has framed, it says "Were you also aware," which tends to suggest that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please perhaps put the question again, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Should we look at a document, 65 ter 1D49, dated the 6th of August. This is from the Croatian Ministry of Defence Main Staff, so headquarters. It's a document from the Chief of the Main Staff, General Cervenko. Presumably, you knew that was his position, General Forand, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that I remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know what position General Cervenko was at all in the Croatian army structure?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. It's an order that concerns you, in many respects, issued on the 6th of August, 9.00. Paragraphs 1 and 2, we need not consider. Paragraph 3: "Once again, I warn all subordinate commanders and order them to be fair to the UNCRO and other UN employees, whose lives and property should not be put at any risk." And: "The military district commanders," "ZP" means military district, "... and others shall personally answer to me for the implementation of this order and draw up a report ..." Were you aware that, in fact, the Chief of Staff had issued a command relating to UNCRO protection of -- for you and your property?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May that be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D322, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D322 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 65 ter number 1958, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is from General Cervenko as well, on the 6th of August, to commanders of the military districts: "Based on information from the areas liberated by the Croatian army, and for the purpose of preventing theft of property and undisciplined conduct, I hereby:" Paragraph 1: "Following entry of army members into the liberated areas, prevent undisciplined conduct." Paragraph 2: "Vigorously prevent the theft of property and war booty. Take vigorous measures against perpetrators of undisciplined conduct." Specific, there, in relation to Croatian army members. Were you aware that orders such as that were issued?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this become an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D323, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D323 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the last order I'm going to look at as example, General Forand, dated the 7th of August, to the commanders of military districts. An order giving various details. It is from General Cervenko from the Main Staff. If we go to page 2, look at paragraph 6: "Take all necessary measures, dedicate yourself fully to the implementation of conduct of military discipline, maintenance of order in the zone of responsibility. Prevent burning, looting, and all other illegal acts." Again, the same form of order relating to the order and discipline of troops. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any discussion between you and your headquarters in Zagreb as to the measures to be taken and discussion to be had at that level at the Main Staff in relation to your complaints concerning the discipline of troops?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, if we can -- I appreciate I'm running out of time, Your Honour, but I will look at 65 ter 881. Can the previous document be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D324, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D324 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document is dated the 10th of August, 1995. It is from the Split military district command, Zadar forward command post, operative group Sibenik, dated the 10th of August. Order on compliance with military disciplinary measures, and it's pursuant to the order by the commander of the Split Military District because of information from the areas liberated, analysis thereof: " ... in order to prevent theft of property, undisciplined conduct, and save human lives," it is ordered. We don't need to look at paragraph 1, but if we look at paragraph 2: "Take all necessary measures and be fully engaged in the implementation of military disciplinary conduct and the maintenance of order in the zone of responsibility. Prevent burning and all other illegal acts. Take resolute measures against anybody who conducts himself or herself in an undisciplined manner." Paragraph 4: "The order shall become effective immediately ... commanders of the directly subordinated units to be in charge of implementation." Those units are named there. Commander Vukic signed it, and page 3 goes on to show the other units. That's the 10th of August at a time when you were making complaints, General Forand. Were you aware, in fact, that the commanders of units were issuing orders not to prevent -- to prevent crimes and undisciplined acts?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did anyone make you aware of the measures that were being taken --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- within the Croatian armed forces, orders that were being issued to prevent crimes and other illegal acts?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's half past 10.00. I know I'm at the end of my allotment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, apparently, you have agreed with other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have an agreement. There were further orders within this sequence of military measures relevant to this issue, Your Honour, which are relevant to the state of mind of this witness and the declarations made by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The type of documents that were shown to you in the last five minutes, are you aware of the existence of any other such, if I could say, internal follow-up documents within the Croatian structures about the matters as dealt with in these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Tieger, I take it that if Mr. Kay wants to produce such documents, that -- from the bar table, that we will hear from you whether there is any objection to it, first of all, as a matter of principle, and then, of course, second to every single document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it as a matter of principle not that you would like to have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They are all Prosecution 65 ter documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, again, the fact that they are from the Prosecution, as such, is not given in itself much weight. The only thing is that, of course, the Prosecution should be aware of the existence of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's that they were to be used in trial, as I understood it from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that diminishes the risk of --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Precisely. I mean, no one is suggesting there's going to be a problem. I would just like to see what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Then, Mr. Kay, there was a similar issue outstanding about a bundle you produced before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to hear the Prosecution's view on that. I already can give a short comment, Mr. Kay, that not all of these documents are translated; therefore, I think if you want to have a full set, that at least every document should be there, and at least in one of the official languages. And since they were all drafted in B/C/S, the originals are there but we can't do without translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not all of them are translated. Many of them are but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They are uploaded, apparently. The Prosecution have been diligent in relation to Your Honours' guidance as to the management of the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They are uploaded, and I anticipate if they've been uploaded, that there will be a translation now in the system. If not, those are matters that we can return to with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- translation department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is this Chamber has no access to uploaded documents, as such, if they are not released. We have a different type of access where you put them at standby for being tendered and admitted. We have no access to your series of documents that are in the waiting cue, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You're lucky, Your Honour, is all I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can usually find my way through an electronic system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The last document, Your Honour -- I am sorry if I crossed Your Honour. I was not being rude. It was just to be to be made an exhibit, so I don't lose my document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger, that was the last one of the examples given.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Forand, we'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are on your feet, may I take it you are the next one to cross-examine Mr. Forand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Forand, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morn, General.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I would like to go through some items that were in your statement starting with the 1996 statement, and go through several issues with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That would be P330.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then talk to you about some of the items that were in your recitation that you gave to the Canadian Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be helpful if I give the hard copy to the witness with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a copy for Your Honours as well as for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of the statement. As well as, there's also an item to be introduced into evidence which is a comparison for the two, which is in e-court at 1D28-0151. So the witness has been given P330 and P401, and a red-lined version which is 1D28-0151. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, if we may, and if we can just briefly take a look at your 1996 statement, which is P130, and go to page 3, we start with you talking about: "Let me turn to the Croatian offensive nicknamed Operation Storm." And if we can go to P401, which is your DEM presentation, and turn to page 18, you can see, General, that the verbiage starting at the top is virtually identical or it is identical, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you -- this presentation to the DEM presentation by you took place on June the 24th, and the interview in P330 took place August 19th and 20th, 1996. Did they -- you provided this to the investigator, Mr. Robertsson, and he essentially wrote this out, did he not, following your presentation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I remember how it went is that I had written that presentation; and when this individual came to query me, I was using the presentation to refer to the questions he was asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And as you look through, even on the first sentence of the paragraph, it's the same exact words, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to go through it to see if, throughout, it's the same exact word, but it was based on my presentation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's do that, then. In that page that we looked at, the first page of page 18 -- or let us start with P330. You note in the first sentence of the second paragraph: "Firstly, there was an orchestrated psychological campaign of troops and equipment movements by the Croatian forces ..." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In your presentation, there is -- the rest of the sentence has been deleted. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in your presentation, it reads, "Firstly, there was an orchestrated psychological campaign of troop and equipment movements by the Croatian force, calculated to keep the ARSK on edge and to mislead them as to their intentions." Now, that last part --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. "Future intentions" is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise "future intentions ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now that last part has been stricken from your statement. When you wrote your presentation to the DEM, did you intend that sentence to be directed towards a psychological campaign against the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that last sentence to mislead them as to their future intention?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You say, in D401, your DEM presentation," ... calculated to keep the ARSK on edge and to mislead them as to their future intentions."

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you were talking about the psychological campaign in your statement, you were talking about a psychological campaign to keep the ARSK, the army, on edge, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: For ease of reference, Your Honour, I may -- we can flip back and forth, but if we can put 1D280-151 on the screen, Judge, that is the statement that I have taken the liberty to red line through, so for ease of reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's certainly assists for comparison reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Frankly, Your Honour, it's difficult at times, so we did this just because of that. We can turn to the next page. I also want to note, Your Honour, that the entire 401 has not been translated because some of it was not, of course, part of -- part of P330 because it had to do with some other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now the second time. I refrained from commenting it the first time; but when you said "it's stricken from your statement," it does not appear in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It does not appear in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's here also, you now said, because of course it was not part of P330. The witness explained that P330 was created by frequent reference to his presentation, but not that it was part of it and not that it ... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let us move down to where it says "thirdly," and move to the bottom of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we go to the next page in the red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the way it reads in your statement to the OTP, it notes: "Even after the fall of Grahovo, it was business as usual in Knin with the few soldiers that were there due to rotation or manning the barracks. They were lounging in bars or shopping in the streets. We saw no defensive position erected, no blocking positions created. A very strange reaction given the overall situation."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the item in P401.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you note in P401, and this is on page 19, that: "Even after the fall of Grahovo, it was business as usual with soldiers lounging in the bars or shopping in the streets." In your statement to the DEM, there is no adjective "few" there. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Likewise, in your statement to the OTP, after it notes that there was a few soldiers, there is the inclusion "that were there due to rotation or manning the barracks." Now, no such description is set forth in your statement to the OTP. You only note that there are soldiers in the town; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what's written there, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you, sir, when you saw these soldiers, really had no idea what they were doing, if they were stationed there or they were moving in and out, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm just letting the translators catch up, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to your statement that you gave to the DEM, you said, "We saw only a small --"

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. It's not a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's a presentation.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a big difference, in my view; and to them, that was a daily executive meeting. That was the chief of defence staff and the three star in the armed forces, but I never gave that -- even though it was slated to be given to them, I never gave that presentation to the daily executive meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. So this was just something that was written by you but never actually presented?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to the daily executive meeting. I presented it maybe three, four times to some of the military that had been with me in Croatia, you know, afterwards as I was moving throughout the country but, it was not presented to the daily executive meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, General. If we can go back to this and go to the next sentence, you say that: "We saw only a small increase of military traffic towards the border." Now, that is not in your 1993 statement to the OTP. Is that accurate, sir, that you did, in fact, see -- excuse me, 1996. Is that accurate that you did, in fact, see an increase in military traffic towards the border?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- how this presentation came about was obviously over a series of months, and some of what I put in there obviously is my own previous reflection, but it was based on information that I possessed at that time. And when we say there was no -- in that instance, it was near Strmica, which was close to the border of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and not too far from Bos Grahovo. And the report I was getting from the Kenyan observation post that was there reflected that they had not seen any increase, you know, in military traffic. That's what I referred to in this particular sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That they had not seen an increase?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go through that. You were aware that in the summer of 1995, the HV had successfully taken -- late July 1995, that the HV had successfully taken Grahovo?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you aware that the HV -- excuse me, that the ARSK was moving troops and supplies up to the Strmica area to counter the HV advances?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you D222.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll go back to the red line in a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is a map, sir, of movement between Knin to Strmica and to the Grahovo area. Are you familiar with this route?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the route, but not this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. And are you -- but you're unfamiliar or you have no knowledge of troops or supplies moving, using that route to augment ARSK forces on the front between Strmica and Grahovo?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
