utterances.text: No, sir. The report that I had during that period was they were ARSK troop moving from Knin towards Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Towards Bihac.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let me turn your attention to D223. General, this is a letter from General Mrksic to General Janvier in Zagreb, protesting shelling on the Drvar-Grahovo-Knin road, and notes this has put in jeopardy the transportation of humanitarian aid. Did you receive this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you receive any information coming from Zagreb that the ARSK was complaining about HV shelling in the Strmica area?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember anything coming from Zagreb, but there was some sitrep where there was some exchange of fire occurring between the ARSK and the HVO troops in that particular area within that time-frame, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did -- I'm just taking a pause between our question and answer. Did you talk to the ARSK about the shelling by the HVO up around -- excuse me, by the HV, in and around the Strmica area?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you: Mr. Jeff Hill, or Captain Hill, was your chief of military police or the head of the military police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was under operational -- my operational control, which meant that I could give him some specific tasks but, he was under operational command of UNCRO. But he was located with his people in our headquarter, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, in latter part of July, Mr. Hill testified that he went up to the Strmica area. And on page 3812, line 21, he notes, this is the question: "Now, were the front lines that you stumbled into ARSK front lines?" Answer: "Yes." Question: "They now had tanks. T-80 and T-84s are the more modern versions of the former JNA tanks, aren't they?" Answer: "It is a designation for the JNA tank. But T-80, for example, was known as the T-72 by NATO Russian, one of their better ones. T-84 is an APC JNA, which is actually a BMP-2 Russian NATO." He talks about is seeing a lot of brass on the road on 3814. "When you noticed that there was a lot of brass on the road, what did you mean by that Captain?" "From their cannons on the APCs, the road was littered with cannon shells. We were actually driving over them." That same page, 3814: "Are these shells coming from the ARSK APCs?" Answer: "Yes." Now, we can go on. Now, did Captain Hill come back and inform you, while he was up, that there were, in fact, military weaponry in that area that was firing into the HVO line?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember Captain Hill briefing me; but as I mentioned earlier, we were aware that there was exchange of fire that had been ongoing in that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just as an aside, you noted for us that you had some control over the military police, and you made a distinction between operational command and operational control. Can you explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operational control is that I can give him some tasks, you know, which he will do for me, like certain inquiry, certain type of specific task. But he was under the command of the UNCRO headquarters which provided him, you know, direct orders, plus administrative support and all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in the latter part of July, you tasked Captain Berikoff to go up to the Strmica area, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I remember that I went myself once because I wanted to ensure that the Kenyan observation post that was there increased their security, because I had given order to all of my people that if ever there was an attack from the Croat side, I wanted them to remain in their observation post and I wanted them to increase their own security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if we can turn to 1D28-0019, which is a excerpt from Captain Berikoff's diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At the top of the page, on 30, 31, 30 July, Sunday: "Up at 0700, another day. Not sure what will happen today. It was quiet last night. Everything tasked to go and spend the night in Strmica with the Kenyans. Very interesting. Saw all kinds of equipment on the way there: BMPs, M-12s, anti-tank gun, M-84 tanks, and everything. Shelling started at 1830 and continued for an hour and a half. Two M-84 tanks crossed border of BH at about 1900. Then one came back a couple of hours later. Many ARSK around the area." If you note on July 31st: "Departed the crossing point at 0630. Returned to Sector South HQ, briefed the General." Do you recall that, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you don't recall sending Captain Berikoff up there?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the sending of Captain Berikoff up there, would that have been because you didn't have faith in the Kenyan Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say it's not because I had faith; it's just to get complementary information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you ultimately wrote to General Gotovina in this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to P336, which is a letter from you to General Gotovina, 31 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Without reading this letter in it's entirety, you bring General Gotovina aware of your UN elements in Strmica. But in this letter, you say nothing about civilians, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, because all I'm talking about is my UN observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I understand. However, if we go to P333, paragraph 4, you note on -- in paragraph 4, you noted: "In late July ..." This is your 2008 statement: "In late July, 1995, the town of Strmica had come under artillery fire from HV/HVO positions in the area of Bosanski Grahovo. In addition to the civilians in that area, there was a KenBat observation post near the border at Strmica." Now, we just noted in P336 that there was no mention of civilians in your letter to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can bring up P337, and if we can go to page 3 of that document -- make that 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And under the miscellaneous paragraph, if we can go to the next page, this is discussing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we stay on the bottom of that page one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can see at the bottom the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Go back to the prior page, just one moment, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we note at the bottom on paragraph 3: "SLO Sector South visited the area the Strmica." This has to do with Colonel Tymchuk's visit to Strmica. If we go to the next page, the top paragraph, about midway through, it notes: "For most of the 70 minutes spent in the area, the sound of artillery could be heard with many projectiles from the Croat side impacting within a kilometre. There were no civilians evident in Strmica." General, do you know when the civilians that had been in Strmica left Strmica?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, throughout the next several days, you received sitreps, did you not, that there was continuous exchange of fire in the Strmica area between the ARSK and the HV, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to recall that, yes, sir. I think it's reflected in the sitrep, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, during this period of time, were you in contact with the ARSK forces in Knin in late July?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, myself, personally. Some of my staff might have been. I don't remember myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that Colonel Tymchuk might have been in contact with him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either Colonel Tymchuk or Colonel Leslie, who was my Chief of Staff at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did either Colonel Leslie or Colonel Tymchuk tell you that, in conversation with the ARSK, that they were planning an offensive known as "Dinara 95" against the HVO to retake Grahovo?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me see if one thing refreshes your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn to D161, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I know you haven't seen this document, General. I just ask if this refreshes your memory. I suspect you haven't seen it. This is an account of the chief logistics officer of the ARSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn to the insert for 30 July 1995, three-quarters down the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just read that, 30 July 1995: "I took part in making plans for attacking Operation Dinara 95. Also 220 soldiers were planned for this operation with the assistance of the RSK, air force and units of the 7th Corps, 15th Corps, and the Special Units Corps. The goal of this operation was to liberate Grahovo in coordination with the VRS," VRS being the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection in this regard at all?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could go back to the red line, which is 1D28-0151.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go back to your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, as well as the DEM presentation, in the last sentence of your OTP statement, you say you saw no defensive positions erected. In your statement -- excuse me. In your presentation, I'm sorry, in your presentation, DEM presentation, you note: "We saw only a small increase of military traffic towards the border, no new defensive positions erected." Now, during the time you were there, were there defensive positions that you observed?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, through your personnel that were travelling in the area?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I had been briefed, when I arrived in the sector, I had been briefed that there was certain defensive positions that were in place, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were these put in place by the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yet in this particular presentation, the word you have "new" has been deleted from your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just think there should be some geographic specificity with that question: Where and what the defensive positions were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can, of course, deal with that in re-examination. But if we could already, if there is a real risk of confusion and mixing up, then you are invited, Mr. Kehoe, to avoid that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can if we can move into the "fourthly" paragraph, in that first in your statement, you note that: "Fourthly, on the RSK side, their continuous hard like taken towards negotiations and the ARSK support of the Bosnian Serb offensive against Bihac from Sector North were pointless actions that only contributed to the sense of hopelessness in the Krajina." The next sentence: "These actions also played into the hands of the Croats by giving them an argument for the military option which in a way, I think, President Tudjman and his Generals wanted ..." Let us turn our attention to the presentation and focus on that last sentence: "These actions also played into the hands of the Croats by giving them a valid argument for the military option. To this day, it is hard to understand the reasoning by those who ordered these actions or did not take the appropriate measures in reaction to the evolving threat. There must be some unknown factors or deals here." Your presentation at the time, in June of 1996, described the Operation Storm, or the beginning of Operation Storm, being premised on a valid argument; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written there, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was written by you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but it was based on my interpretation. You know that made it clear when I made that presentation that was based, you know, of what I had been -- what I had seen and what was my interpretation of what had happened, and it was not based on all complete and full proof.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. Let us continue on, on this score.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, General, just looking at P330, the OTP statement, who typed this?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This statement that the Office of the Prosecutor -- that you signed for the Office of the Prosecutor, who typed this?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us continue on, and we go to the paragraph starting at the bottom, "I truly believe," that carries on to the next page. It notes: "I truly believe that by the eve of war, the Krajina had been psychologically defeated. I am not a proponent of certain propaganda line that the HV are a powerful professional force." Just starting from there, General, you knew that this was an army that had just begun, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had been formed approximately a year or so prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Most of their attacks were uncoordinated and went nowhere. It was not obvious that they have mastered the tactics of interaction of combat arms. The use of artillery was excellent when being used against military targets." Let us stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn back to Exhibit 401.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And on page 20 of 45 at the top paragraph, the sentence that you have is, the top paragraph, that: "The use of artillery was excellent, but the coordination between artillery, tanks, and infantry was not evident." Now, what's included in the OTP statement that's not included in your presentation is the following: "Their use of artillery was excellent when being used against military targets; however, the artillery was, to a large extent, used against villages and towns like Knin, and not against targets in the zone of separation. This shelling created mass panic among the population and forced it to leave." Now, we see, first, that the -- your description in your presentation, as you wrote it in your presentation, was meant to be a complement on the accuracy of HVO artillery fire, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not so sure if it was meant to be perceived as complement, but that's the way I wrote it there. But I think I explained a little bit later on, you know, where the shelling has taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, suffice it to say, that you noted that it was excellent?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you -- going on to the sentence following, you don't include in your presentation that: "... the shelling created mass panic among the population and forced it to flee." That's in page 20 in your presentation at the top.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I wrote later on why the Serbs did not shell the Croatian city, as the HV were doing to them. I mean, what you have here in my statement, you know, is a very condensed of what was in my presentation. I think you have to go through the whole presentation if you want to make those type of relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's continue on. What's also left out, if we move on and stay in your presentation, starting with the paragraph of: "However, we have to recognise that the Croatians had tremendous strategic success and that their small special force units did successfully accomplish special missions." Now, that particular sentence is not included in the statement to the OTP. Now, would you consider that to be a complementary statement for the HV?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you make the decision not to include it in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think that I wilfully exempted certain things from my deposition that was in my presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, did you give this statement to Mr. Robertsson, and he retyped this and gave it back to you to sign [Realtime transcript read in error "resign"]?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's continue on. After you note that the Croats don't possess a professional army, this is the overall sentence, it notes in your OTP statement: "I believe that the Croatians do not possess a professional army or have developed a capability to utilise the combat power to its full extent. The result may have been different had the ARSK not stripped some of its resources in Bihac, but instead prepared second and third defence lines especially in the areas that favour this, and would have been able to sustain the fear of the HV, the HV artillery attacks against villages and towns, especially Knin, instead of panicking and evacuating the civilian population." Now, let us turn to your presentation on that score. After you note again that, I believe, verbatim: "I believe that the Croatians do not possess a professional army or have developed the capability to utilise combat power to its full extent. The results may have been quite different had the ARSK not tripped some of its resources to unducate the Bihac offensive, or had not taken the decision on 4 August to order the withdrawal of the civilian population from Sector South. By this last action, the RSK appeared to be giving up and inevitably initiated the general retreat that followed." Now, General, that passage, we've noted, is not included in your OTP statement; and in that statement, you maintain that the decision to evacuate - and I don't want to put words in your mouth, General; you can correct me if I am wrong - the decision to evacuate was the trigger that initiated the general retreat that followed, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was certainly a great factor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Robertsson retyped this for you, General, he did not include that sentence in your statement to the OTP, did he?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I have some -- Mr. Kehoe, one of your earlier questions was: "General, did you give this statement to Mr. Robertsson, and he retyped this and gave it back to you to" sign, I take it. It says "resign." But, first of all, it talks about the statement. Do I have to understand your testimony to be that you gave your written presentation --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Presentation, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to Mr. Robertsson?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I gave it to him, sir, or if I was referring to my presentation when he was asking me question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, you earlier said: "I don't know who typed it." And in this answer, you say, "He retyped this," which suggests that you would know who typed the statement as given to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did I just say that, that he retyped this? I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was part of a question. The question was: "General, did you give this statement," and apparently Mr. Kehoe had on his mind his presentation to Mr. Robertsson, "and he retyped this and gave it back to you to," I take it you said "sign." Then your answer was: "Yes, sir."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, this DEM presentation was received from the Office of the Prosecutor as part of -- coming from the Canadians -- excuse me, signed by General Forand, and as an exhibit to one of his statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you mean. He identified it as --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, still, the retyping is rather unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will clarify it, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you please do so, because I'm a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, the presentation that you put together for 24 June 1996, you gave this to the OTP -- the Office of the Prosecutor's investigator, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was in 1996 or 1997, but they have a copy of it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when your statement was written that you signed, P330, you -- were you the person who typed this or did one of the investigators type it before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't type it. I think the statement was taken on a tape and it was sent back to me, you know, to verify, you know, if it was what I had said, and I signed it; and if I remember well, I sent it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With all due respect, General, I think you're talking about the second statement that was on tape.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There was an awful --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There was a statement that was on tape, in fairness, General.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was the first one? I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, if we can continue on, on this score --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I still try to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What Mr. Kehoe is putting to you is that there is a striking resemblance of major portions of your August 1996 statement compared to the 24th of June presentation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Many lines just the same, apparently portions taken out, portions added. First of all, the 24th of June, 1996 presentation, had you typed it out your is self or did you have an electronic copy available to yourself? The presentation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not type it personally, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was typewritten for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was typewritten, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have an electronic copy of the text?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever provide that electronic copy to the persons who interviewed you two months later, mid-August 1996.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir, and I don't remember if I gave them that copy in 1996 or in 1997, you know. When it was provided to them, I don't remember. But, in all likelihood, if it was provided, I would have given them also an electronic copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now when you signed this August 1996 statement, did you read it carefully again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last question on this issue: The presentation, you said you didn't type it out. Did you give the formulations? I mean was it that you wrote it down in handwriting, or I mean if someone else typed it out, was it on the basis of what you had dictated in a machine or written down on paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The way it started, sir, it was a Major Balfour, and I had told him I wanted to prepare something on my return to Canada. I gave him the headings that needed to be covered, and I said start on this. So it was a working document that took almost a year to be completed when I returned to Canada. But Major Balfour had started to collect all the slides, the photo, and all of that. So he gave me a CD. When I came back home, I started to put it together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in your presentation that we just read on page 20, concerning the evacuation, you don't use the word - and I'm talking about the second paragraph on page 20 - you don't use the word "panicking" or "evacuating," do you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not there, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can continue on, on this, this is another matter that is paragraph -- if we go down to the paragraph, "To this day ..." In your presentation, it notes: "To this day, there are questions to which I have no answers. Why was there no second line of defence prepared, especially when the ground favours it? The only military aim that the ARSK could have had to buy time demanded it." Now, again, that is not in your OTP statement, and my question is on the issue of buying time. What were you talking about, General, with the ARSK buying time? Now we're talking about your page 20 of 45 of your presentation.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in order for them, you know, to be able to further develop their defensive position, which they had not done at this particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, if they had a second and third line defence position, your testimony is that that would have bought them some time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they would have been able to block the HV attack, you know, when that would have happened, then, obviously, the longer it would have taken the Croat to retake the Krajina, the more time maybe, you know, some external organisation or country would have step up and say, "Okay, let's stop the fighting and resume the discussion." That's what I had in mind there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just to flesh that out a bit, General, were you contemplating the Bosnian Serb army or the JNA intervening to come to the aid and assistance of the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, that's not what I had in mind there. All I was trying to portray, if they had developed, you know, secondary defensive position which the terrain, from my point of view, allowed them to do, they could have stopped potentially the attack, and potentially, you know, the discussion for peace would have resumed. That was what I meant by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who did you have in mind was going to come in and intervene?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intervene? Well, the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move on in the statement, if we may, and if we can go back to the 1D28-0051, the red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, General, following up on what you just said, waiting for the UN to intervene. You were the UN.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't think I had that type of authority. I was referring back to my experience in 1974 in Cyprus, where after the initial Turkish attack, there was a lull in the battle that was imposed by the United Nations before it resumed. So, in my mind, you know, if there was sufficient capability for the ARSK to defend, potentially the UN may have put some pressure on both sides to resume the peace. So that's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there discussion about that, that, in fact, if there was some battle that was resisted, that the UN would, in fact, intervene to bring about a secession of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to your presentation, and I will take you through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I apologise if I jump and a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I want to turn to page 22 of your presentation, and I believe that will go -- begins the paragraph, "The first successful area ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah, that's it. If we can go to the red line up a couple of pages. At the red line, it starts with, "The first successful area," at the top. It's 1D28-0151 and page 6 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, we actually have -- this is, as you can see, much -- starting of that has been stricken, but let's just go through this very quickly. We're talking about events on the 4th: "The first area is the successful penetration in the south-east by HV 10 company when they came over the Dinara mountains from Bosnia. This was during the 4 August around 10.00 a.m. ..." And we now move into a discussion of a particular area that is not in the statement, and I take it from the presentation 401, page 22: "This was done during 4 August around 10.00 a.m., and the question of the lack of ARSK defences in the area must be revisited. The Serbs were well aware of the threat, especially following the fall of Grahovo, but did not react to defend, block, or counter it. As soon as the penetration began, the ARSK abandoned their positions at Maljkovo and fled without blocking a six-kilometre portion of road, which was the ideal choke point for reserve demolitions or blocking positions. This gave the HV the opportunity to link up their force advancing from the south and reinforce on a major route." Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, minor correction. Again, just to get the record straight; not "the ideal" but "an ideal."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Apologies. Thank you. "An ideal."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, taking a look at that, General, I would like to bring an item up on the screen because you talk about Maljkovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's 1D28-0173 -- 74, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is a -- one of the slides from your outline that has Maljkovo present there; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the area that you're talking about that is north of the lake that was the choke point; right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let me go to the next map, which is 0173, the one we just had up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, I have an item on the screen. As you can see, Maljkovo is not on the north part of the lake but on the south part of the lake, and it appears from your map that you were, in fact, talking about the choke point at Vrlika; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, from the area of Maljkovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, General, but your prior map on Maljkovo had Maljkovo north of the lake?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the precise map, you know, it was end round.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Maljkovo is, in fact, all the way down at the bottom of the lake.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you, in fact, talking about Vrlika?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking from the direction of Maljkovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, do you see where Maljkovo is on the map?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, so, your position is that you were talking about the -- when you were dealing with your map, you were talking about the Maljkovo at the bottom of that page? General, if looking at the map, the choke point of the convergence of these roads is in Vrlika, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To me, I was saying is that there were some defensive positions at Maljkovo, which they fled, they didn't stay there. So whatever was coming from the south was able to link up with the 10 company that came in from the east in the Dinara. That's all I'm saying in what you see on my presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, were you familiar with the ARSK positions in Vrlika?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Familiar, in what sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you know of those ARSK positions in Vrlika?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some, yes, but I'm not that familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I just want to ask you, given your testimony, that Vrlika is in the Cetina valley, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you stated during the course of your direct testimony, at page 4117: Question: "Did you see any evidence of Serb weaponry or positions in the area where the shelling was taking place or where the harvest was being prevented?" Answer: "No. I did what I would think or qualify as a complete tour of the area, and I didn't see none of those weapons." Now, how many times did you actually travel in the Cetina Valley, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was around -- it was in July. It must have been around the 11th or 12th of July. It's in the sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And sir, during that period of time, there were, in fact, restrictions of movement transpiring in the Cetina Valley by the ARSK, right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I remember, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you have -- you had restrictions of movement by the ARSK during that time, sir, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go back to your statement, if we can, 401 -- the presentation, excuse me. 401, page 10, third paragraph from the top: "The army of the republic of Serb Krajina or ARSK were better known to us as we dealt with them on a daily basis. Nonetheless, we only had a superficial appreciation of their strengths and weaknesses as they also restricted our movements. And following the 1st May attack of Sector West, they had withdrawn all of their equipment from the storage -- weapons storage area, therefore inhibiting our accounting and verification of their assets." So, after May the 1st, did you have restriction of movement in the Cetina valley?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the Cetina valley. You are asking me specifically if it was restricted. I don't remember that. When went over there, I was restricted to go around the whole area. This statement that you've just read in my presentation meant that certain areas we could not go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where could you not go?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this also notes - and when I say "this," I'm talking about your presentation - that: "The ARSK had withdrawn all their equipment from the storage area, therefore inhibiting our accounting and verification of their assets." So it would be accurate to say that you don't know what kind of weaponry the ARSK had; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe not me specifically; but before I had arrived, the United Nations had been there for a certain period of time. I think I they had a certain knowledge of what the ARSK possess. You've got to remember also that my mandate was in the zone of separation, plus the 13 Croat village and the four crossing border point. The responsibility on monitoring the equipment on both side was of the military observer responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, in July -- and let me again give you the testimony of Mr. Hill, Captain Hill, page 3809. He testified here on the 28th of May, talking about the equipment in the Cetina Valley: "The equipment, this heavy equipment, heavy artillery pieces and tanks that you saw in and around Vrlika, can you explain with a little more specificity, Captain, exactly, what you say?" Answer: "When we say "tanks," it would be T-54s or T-72s, NATO designation; APCs; MP-2s; and the artillery would be towed at 130 millimetre." Now, did Captain Hill tell you about that equipment that he observed in the Cetina valley in late July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I note that the answer, or the question, didn't specify a time period, and I thought that would be obviously helpful to the question and potential answer. But I think, after I rose, I think Mr. Kehoe mentioned it was in late July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the matter is moot. Please proceed. Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the typing; it's marked 28th of May. I arrive only -- I took over on the 8th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, General. That's his testimony, 28th of May, 2008. That's when he testified here. I apologise if I wasn't clear. That's what he testified to when he was here on 28th May.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: So which date are you referring that he saw that equipment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He says in late July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It says -- according to the question posed to you, it says: "At the end of the July, he noted that ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Late July, end of July. I apologise --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I just think that references to the document seem preferable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I went there, sir, I didn't see that particular equipment, and I don't recall Captain Hill briefing me on that. It's possible, but I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the UNMOs in the area, there was a Mr. Tchernetsky that testified that: "There was an anti-aircraft gun, an anti-aircraft artillery ..." -- This is what he says on page 3270 line 3: "In Kijevo, also in the Cetina valley, there was an anti-aircraft artillery piece, an anti-aircraft gun. It was either 57- or 76-millimetres in calibre. I cannot remember exactly." Did you know about that particular item?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you learn or do you recall any military positions that the ARSK had in the Cetina valley at all?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to visit the Kenyan observation post, there was some offensive position in the Dinara mountain that the ARSK occupied, but I don't remember seeing any major equipment, heavy equipment, in that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would come from the -- the one occasion that you were there?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in your letter to General Gotovina - by the way, I mean just to speed through this - there was, in fact, a secession of shelling to allow the harvest to continue; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had written the second letter, yeah, there was a period of time, I think a couple of weeks, where there was no shelling that took place, to allow the people to gather the -- what was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right. And let me just turn your attention to P334, and I'm talking about the last paragraph. This is a letter to General Gotovina, 9 July 1995. You note in the last paragraph: "I remain determined to reach a negotiated settlement to the hostilities in the Dinara Mountains area, including the withdrawal of Serb heavy weapons to storage sites." Did you do that, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I do what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get a withdrawal of Serb heavy weapons to storage sites?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Like I said there, that was my intention; and, again, you know, when I went to visit, I didn't see any. That doesn't mean they were not somewhere else, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And staying on that score, if you have a piece of artillery that is mobile, it can be taken from one location to another; right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, just because you didn't see it, doesn't mean they didn't have it in the area?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, earlier, at least that's how it appears on the transcript, is that the testimony by Mr. Tchernetsky would have been: "It was an anti-aircraft artillery police and an anti-aircraft gun." That, I don't know how you pronounced it, but it's not the word "and," but it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I meant "an," A-N, Judge. Not two weapons, I meant one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That appears from the transcript, just to be correct, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's us go back to 1D28-0151, which is the red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, if we could look at the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think if we can go to two pages up, please. I'm sorry, just one page back, please. We're looking at the bottom paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, we're talking about the period of time, General, when you are going down to see the ARSK authorities. We start with the area that says: "During the whole day, shelling into populated areas had created panic among the RSK leadership and population. The RSK Supreme Defence Counsel took a decision to evacuate the towns and villages sometime during the 4 August 1995. The hierarchy asked for a meeting at 1800 in Knin. And that evening, the 4 August, General Mrksic was not there, but I met his Chief of Staff and five RSK ministers. They appeared totally confused and in a panic." Now let us turn back to your presentation which is P401. You note, starting in that paragraph, "During the night ..." It says: "The whole day -- they included the whole day. Shelling into populated areas had created panic among the RSK leadership." Then you note: "Given the relatively stable situation, and with the penetration that could be blocked or at least tried to be contained, one must ask why the RSK decided to order the civilian population to flee, unless it was an already foregone conclusion" -- excuse me, "decision." Now, you described -- you, initially, got to the RSK headquarters approximately 11.30, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 4th, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you got there, you were of the belief that the situation was, in fact, stable; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the information I was receiving from my unit, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And "stable," tell us what you mean by "stable"?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there was no inroad specifically, you know, across the whole front. There was some -- I don't know if that time -- I think the 10 company -- I may not have known, because as soon as the 10 company from the Dinara moved, the Kenyan command post lost contact with that company of Kenyans that was in that area. And coming through the Velebit, I'm not sure if I had that information when I met that ARSK colonel in the morning there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And by "stable," you mean that the ARSK forces weren't panicking and fleeing; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Stable" meant, you know, that the front was holding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now continuing on with this -- by the way, this situation, as you described the situation on the morning of the 4th, when you go to the ARSK headquarters and you describe the entire matter as a stable situation, that was not included in your statement to the Prosecutor; right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, because I had forgotten about that particular meeting, and I only realised that there had been a meeting when I saw the sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, in fact -- sir, in fact, prior to the drafting of your 1996 statement, you provided the Office of the Prosecutor with the presentation that we have in 401; right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier, I don't remember if it was at that time that they were provided. They would have to tell you that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move, continue on with this, staying with your presentation at, "I understand now ..." And we're on page 23, last paragraph. "I understand now that the RSK Supreme Defence Council took the decision at about noon on 4 August to abandon the Krajina." Now, the RSK, sir, made that decision at a time when you assessed the military situation to be stable, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I've been trying to follow this, and if there is a reference to the previous paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll give you the page; it's page 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do see that but the continual references to the General's assessment of the stability of the situation in his presentation has been linked to the morning meeting and doesn't seem to say that there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think we can certainly clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, at the time that you got to the RSK headquarters on the morning of the 4th of August, did you consider the military situation to be stable?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the information that I had at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you got there at approximately 11.00, 11.30?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is in the situation report, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You subsequently learned that the RSK made a decision on noon of the 4th of August to, as you say, abandon the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information came from the refugee that came into my camp, and I learned about that a couple of weeks after the 4th. That was the timing, you know, that they were talking about, but I never verified that particular timing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continuing on about the subsequent meeting, you note in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor -- and I'm talking about the paragraph beginning "during ," and you're talking about the meeting at 1800 hours: "General Mrksic was not there, but I met his COS and five ministers. They appeared totally confused and in panic." Now, again, we have the word "panic." And, again, if we turn our attention back to your presentation, while you use the words "totally confused and mostly incoherent," the word "panic" is not used. My question is: Is the word "panic" a word that you used, sir, or was it a word that Mr. Robertsson included?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it must have been me, but when -- from my understanding of English, confusion and incoherent, you know, it's panic from my point of view. So if I had not used the same word, I mean, if you ask me that question today and another question tomorrow on the same subject, I may use different word, but to me it meant about the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us continue on, on that paragraph, and you continue on and you say -- you see "Their aim"? You say: "Their aim of the meeting was to request that the UN supply 450 trucks and 70.000 litres of fuel to evacuate 30.000 civilians from Knin and the surrounding areas that night. They could not explain how this evacuation would be done, where these people were to be evacuated to, or what resources were available. There was simply no plan."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't know if you want me to break here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this would be a suitable moment for you, we would have a break now. If you would take one or more two minutes, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, it will take a little bit more than that. This is a suitable point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps otherwise it would become too late. We'll take a break and resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At the outset, General, my apologies if I'm moving quickly through this. This is a lot of material, and I know these discrepancies are not your fault. It's just I have to get through a certain amount of material in a certain amount of time. So if it moves quickly, my apologies, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not moving quickly enough for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think the sentiments that you have in that would be expressed by Judge Orie in a different form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I just want to show you before we move into the next area of the statement a video clip, and it is P398. This is by HTV.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "It is hard to understand why the ARSK did not put up a better battle, especially ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "It is hard to understand why the ARSK did not put up a better battle, especially the ground favours the defender, and we know, you know, that the Croats were able to offend them in the south-eastern part of this sector. But still there was a lot of other places where they could have made a stand, and it was not made. Also, one of the things that surprised me from the military point of view is that there was no depth in their defence, no second line or third line. And this is a bit surprising when we look at it from the military point of view. Another aspect that was critical, I think, in their -- why it went so fast is that they decide very early, on the 4th in the afternoon, to evacuate the civilians from Knin and all the surrounding town. And as soon as that was known, everybody start to flee away, including the military."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, General, that evacuation order in around noon that we talked about was critical to the giving up or the defeat of the Krajina, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sure was, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted in your statement to the Prosecutor, that there was no plan. I note, just as we move through this, those words are not in your presentation in P401, and I would like to show you a video. This is 1D15-0065. As this is cueing up, I point to the point that part of your statement where you said that: "These people didn't know where they were going to be evacuated to or what resources were available. There was simply no plan." If we could play this, and this is General Kosta Novakovic of the ARSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- while cueing this other item up, on the issue of no plan and not knowing where they're going, can I show you D182.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can bring up D182 while we're waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Kehoe, you were talking about "the evacuation order in around noon that you talked about." May I take it that you were referring to what was called "the decision on noon to abandon the Krajina"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not linguistically not exactly the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is a memo that went to Sector South headquarters, and I will tell you for the sake of clarity that the parties have agreed that the date in this document is incorrect, and it is 4 August 1995. So to the extent that it says "8 July," the parties have agreed that it is, in fact, "4 August." In the middle part of this document, it talks about a meeting on 1800 to 900 [sic]. And the second paragraph it notes that: "The RSK authorities have requested UN assistance in organising and providing transport for such evacuation. RSK initial calculation shows that UN will node to provide for these refugees transportation around 70 litres -- excuse me, 70.000 litres of fuel, 450 trucks. RSK proposed one main route: From Knin to Padjene, Otric, Srb, Martin Brod, Bosanski Petrovac, Banja Luka. Population from Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac will not pass Knin, but directly through Padjene without directly passing Knin." "The sector commander told RSK that he will request Zagreb authorities, in general, he will recommend this UN support." Do you recall this, General, that there was a plan to follow a particular route as set forth in this document?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, sir. My impression of that meeting was they had no plan at all, and my recollection was for them to provide me a plan before I could be in a position to say what type of help to be provided. I remember that I mentioned that that help because I had reduced capability. I would have been obliged to go back to my headquarters. Once I had known their plans, but there was no plan as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another video. This is for Drago Kovacevic, 1D17-0383, who was a key RSK official at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This sound is not very pleasant. We see an English translation, apparently, of the words spoken by the person we see on the screen. We can proceed in two ways. Either the parties agree that this is a, and perhaps later can verify, that this is an accurate translation of the words spoken. Then we could put our volume very, very low, and then rather read. Otherwise, you have to prepare a better audio for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. I don't know why this isn't working this way. It worked fine before. But the booths have been provided a translation of this -- a transcript, excuse me, of this. So I will take Your Honour's guidance and the Prosecutor's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure either one of the expedients suggested, it seems to me, can work. I don't know if the transcript is of the words spoken by the person on the video himself or is a transcription of what appears in the subtitles. If it's the latter, then we might as well just go forward without the sound and look at what's on the screen. If it's the former, that does sound like it's a potentially more accurate way to proceed, and then we can double-check it as the Court suggested later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have transcripts in the original language and the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we might check one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Not for this particular video clip, the booths do not have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No transcript at all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We do have some but not for this particular video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The booth informs me that they have no transcript for this particular video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's in B/C/S. We have a transcript in English in e-court, but there is no transcript in B/C/S because the people are speaking in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But with this audio quality, no one can verify the words spoken in B/C/S. So, therefore, under those circumstances, either the parties agree sooner or later on on what is on the original perhaps by using other equipment to verify and then to agree on that. And if, Mr. Tieger, if you would engage in such an exercise, then we perhaps could at this moment just look at the video and that you tender English transcript, and the parties could agree on whether the original and the English transcript reflects the words spoken in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then what we do at this moment: We look at the video, we put our volumes low, and the English transcript will then be tendered together with the video, and the parties will reach an agreement on the original words spoken. If that is agreeable, then let's move on this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I think we're finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we first assign a number to the video and then to the English transcript. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D326.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As discussed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that verification of the original should still take place. Then D326 is admitted into evidence with the proviso that within seven days, the Prosecution has an opportunity to revisit the issue of the original words spoken. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I know it's been some time, but did you recognise the bald gentleman that has a hair line like mine, Mr. Kovacevic, the mayor of Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the second individual, Colonel Kosta Novakovic, with glass, had you met him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: His face seems familiar, but I'm not sure if I met him or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I know it's been a long time, General. And the last individual, the older man with the grey hair without the glasses, General Sekulic, did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another document sir, which is 1D25-0098. General, this is a cable sent by Mr. Akashi to Mr. Annan, through Mr. Stoltenberg, dated 4 August 1995, and the area that we have -- are interested in is the second page, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just blow up paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "We have been advised by the civil affairs office in Sector South that the Knin leadership have requested UNHCR and UNPF assistance in evacuating 32.000 civilians from Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, and Knin to Petrovac and Banja Luka in Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, General, this was on the 4th of August that Mr. Akashi is sending this from Zagreb to New York. I'm looking if you can help us as to how Mr. Akashi got the details of this plan that Sector South was unaware of or that you were unaware of?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no timing on that, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The only timing we have, sir, is on page 1.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there's only a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There's an incoming time cable, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the front page and if we can circle the right corner, it notes at 2002.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That makes sense, sir, because I had that meeting at approximately 1800 hours. Mr. Al-Alfi was with me, and it reflects what I told you earlier, that since they had no plan, I did not commit myself, and I would say, "Give me your plan." I would have to go back to my headquarter, you know, with that plan. The only thing I offered at that time was some fuel for certain people, and it was a limited amount, you know, that would pass beside my headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When we are talking about times and when we are talking about apparently internationally-sent documents, then it might be interesting to know what kind of time we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge. The top one, it looks like UNPROFOR at the top stamp of 1947.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe, Judge, based on and having dealt with these documents, that it goes out on the current time that you're in. So, as the General noted, that would be consistent with his meeting at 1800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The time you're in depends on who you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you are a receiver, when you are a sender. So I take it that you do not put any time you're not in on a document, but, of course, it depends on where you are, perhaps, and what your role in the whole thing is. But let's move on and keep this in the back of our minds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think, just to clarify this, any way we look at this cable, General, it's after your meeting with the RSK authorities?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we stay on that paragraph 4, it notes that: "There is a wide range of political" -- excuse me, "... policy, political, military, and logistical implications that must be first examined with UNHCR before we can contemplate such a commitment. Accordingly, Sector South has been advised by UNCRO to make no commitment to Knin authorities, other than that the matter will be examined tomorrow." Now, General, with regard to this particular item, making no commitment to the Knin authorities, I mean you made no commitment to evacuate anyone, but you did make a decision, nonetheless, to give them fuel?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for those civilian that would pass beside my headquarters; I stress "civilian."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, also, did you receive a request from Colonel Kosta Novakovic to take civilians into the camp on the night of the 4th?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There is a colonel that came at my gate, if I remember well, around 2300 hours, and that he wanted to -- for me to take into my camp the wounded and the sick from the hospital and I told him no. But I don't remember if it was Novakovic; it was a colonel that I had met previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Colonel Kosta Novakovic told the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal, in his statement in 2001 at page 10, where he actually says: "Our delegation requested the UN to open the gates of the compound to permit the civilians to enter. This was agreed to and the gates were opened." Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gates for the refugees from open, yes, sir. But I think it must have been after I came back from that meeting in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But was it at the request of the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I'm trying to remember if it was at the demand of the -- the request of the ARSK, or if it was Colonel Leslie, you know, that came to me and said, "There's a certain number of people outside the gate and they want to come in. So what is your decision?" And after I thought a while after that, a little while, I said, "Okay. Let them in, and we will accommodate them."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, along the idea of the plan, and going back to your presentation, you note in your presentation -- and I turn our attention to the top of page 2545 -- excuse me, page 25 of 45. Now, the issue of how people got that information is -- the people got the information that there was an evacuation order is answered by you at that passage at the top of the page, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I got from the people that were in the camp, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you note that: "From talking to locals who became refugees in my headquarters, the stories from whose later hear heard from refugees now in Serbia, we know that the withdrawal order was passed by the civil defence organisation as part of the heritage of the socialist police state. There was an existing and well developed civil defence organisation. Everybody," excuse me, "everyone had a block warden, a designated survival area, evacuation routes ..." Now, sir, that portion or that -- that was your understanding as to the communication network that was existing, that was informed of this evacuation order, so they could evacuate pursuant to the decision of the RSK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's the information, as I said, that was provided to me by the refugee in my camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that particular item about how this information was laid out to the civilian population indicated to you in relatively organised communication network that went back to the socialist era; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they had some way of communicating, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That communication item - and I don't blame you for this not being in here, General - but it hasn't been included in your witness statement of 1996, has it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could I seek one clarification. In the presentation, you say that: "From talking to the locals who became refugees in my headquarters and the stories from those who later heard from refugees ..." One of your answers was put on the record a minute ago and reads: "Yeah. That's the information, as I said, that was provided to me by the refugee in my camp." That suggests one person; whereas, your presentation suggests more persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was more than one, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, changing subjects for one moment and just discussing, if we could, the 4th, and if we can move back in our time-frame just a bit. You had a meeting with the RSK, you told us, before noon and then some place around 1800 or something like that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had there been contacts between UNCRO and the RSK or the ARSK prior to that day -- prior to that time that day? The first meeting, I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me ask -- just go through a couple of items on this, and again, talking about the statement of Mr. Kosta Novakovic, Colonel Kosta Novakovic of the ARSK. In his statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on April 5, 2001, he noted on page 9: "On 4 August 1995, at 0400, I was awoken by our liaison officer who said it would be desirable for me to come to our headquarters because the situation was serious. The liaison officer then told me that he had information from a responsible official from UN Sector South headquarters that the Croatian attack will commence at 0500." Let me just touch on one other item, and this is from Mr. Sekulic's book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It should be -- it should be number 20 on our table. It should be 1D28-1009 to 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is from ARSK General Sekulic's book that he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just for clarity, 1D28-0109. The next page, I think. It will be the following page. No, that's not it. It should be at 1D28-0013 -- 0113, my apologies. It is from the same book, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm starting on page 173, General, at "Information that the ..." This is General Sekulic talking about the beginning of Operation Storm. "Information that the aggression would commence on 04 August at 5.00 a.m. had been coming in from various sources. Early in the afternoon on 03 August, information was also provided by the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army. It was then confirmed by the General Staff of the army of the Republika Srpska. The information about the time of the beginning of the operation had come in from various UNPROFOR (UNCRO) sources as well. The officers from the international peace forces appeared to have been competing with one another to provide information about the time of the beginning of the aggression to organs of the Serb army of the Krajina. "After midnight, i.e., early in the morning of 04 August until 5.00 a.m., the operational centre of the army of the Serb Krajina received several calls from the UNPROFOR officers who were at the southern barracks in Knin. They were informing us about the beginning of the aggression in the RSK. Similar information had been coming in through state security channels and other organs of the RSK." I have one last item before I begin to ask you questions on these items and that would come from a video 1D15-0065.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It appears we have the is same difficulty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we then resolve it in a similar way as well or do you need the sound here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we can resolve it in the same fashion, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's decided that we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is, again, Colonel Kosta Novakovic and General Sekulic who have said, both in writing and on these videos, that they were being provided information from UN Sector South. Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had anybody informed you that they were, in fact, informing you them of that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I would have put a stop to that, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, there was a point in time, General -- and, certainly, before I move into the next question, certainly, if they had been provided that information prior to the attack, that would have been a violation of the UN mandate, would it not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sure would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the day, you note in your 1996 statement at paragraph 4, page 5, fourth paragraph, that: "We had provided them," meaning the RSK. For the purpose of coordinating a humanitarian assistance, you provided them a radio; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at my meeting at 1800 hours, if I recall, on the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, when we talk about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can turn our attention to P343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Kehoe, before we do so, I take it that you wanted to tender the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- previous? Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number to the last video and the transcript, the English transcript attached to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D327 is admitted into evidence under the proviso that the Prosecution can verify the original language spoken and may come back with this matter to the Chamber within seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd also like to offer the book excerpt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah.
